title: JFrog Shai-Hulud Here We Go Again npm and PyPI campaign
summary: Source-backed emergency campaign advisory for the May 19, 2026 Shai-Hulud wave reported by JFrog, including npm lifecycle execution, optional GitHub dependency abuse, credential theft, GitHub dead-drop exfiltration, and a related PyPI import-time loader.

safe_versions: Use a version outside the affected range after verifying upstream maintainer guidance and clean lockfiles.
Use a version outside the affected range after verifying upstream maintainer guidance and clean lockfiles.

detection_rationale: npm packages use install-time lifecycle execution, Bun, and non-registry GitHub optional dependency delivery.
PyPI durabletask uses import-time execution to fetch and launch a Python zip payload without executing package code during SecOpsAI analysis.
The campaign includes credential harvesting, GitHub token abuse, GitHub dead-drop exfiltration, persistence, and cloud/Kubernetes lateral-movement indicators.
remediation: Block affected package versions in package-manager policy, artifact proxies, and CI allowlists.
Isolate affected developer workstations and CI/CD runners before revoking GitHub tokens when destructive token monitors may be present.
Remove listed persistence artifacts and hunt for listed domains, files, GitHub dead-drop repository activity, and workflow injection.
Rotate GitHub, npm, PyPI, cloud, Kubernetes, Vault, SSH, CI/CD, and package-manager credentials after host isolation and persistence removal.
